### F-105 — The realm template duplicated the RBAC merge handler instead of reusing it

> _2026-08-18 · core/blong-kopi · resolved_

The blong-core skill documents the RBAC merge seed pattern (`accessAuthorizationMerge` reusing
`core.triple.merge`, with non-dotted capability names) and blong-realm points at it. The template
now reuses the shared handler in code, not just in docs: it ships
`meta/dbTest/accessAuthorizationMerge.yaml` with a fixed filename and deliberately NO `$subject`
placeholder, because the seed method is derived from the filename (`access.authorization.merge`) and
lands on blong-access's shared `accessAuthorizationMerge` handler attached to the `db` adapter. The
earlier `adapter/db/$subjectAuthorizationMerge.ts` duplicate handler was deleted; only the seed
CONTENT carries `$subject` placeholders.

### F-302 — A token substitution rewrote an English word

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-kopi · resolved_

To turn kukum output into the kopi template I replaced the literal names with the dollar tokens, and
the object token was entry. That replaced the word entry inside a generated comment, so the
scaffolded realm read The composed order, not the composed entry. Substituting a common English word
is only safe per token pair in the file paths and identifiers, never as a blanket replace across
prose; the fix was to phrase the comment without the word. Verify a scaffolded realm by reading the
output, not by trusting the substitution.

Fixed: the comment in .storybook/preview.tsx no longer contains the word entry, and a scaffolded
realm was read back to confirm the tokens land as intended.

### F-305 — The generated Open story opened a record the fixture did not have

> _2026-09-28 · core/blong-kopi · resolved_

The storybook descriptor emits page of subject object open with record 1, so the story renders a
form for record 1, but the template fixture shipped the rows from the DB seed, whose first key is
101 — the story therefore opened a record that does not exist and rendered an empty form while every
file involved looked right. Two lessons. The descriptor cannot know a realm fixture keys, so its
notice now says the Open record must exist in the fixture. And the fixture and the seed are
independent sources for the same sample rows: the template fixture now keys its rows 1 and 2 so its
own story shows data, and both files say which path each one feeds. Recorded and fixed in the same
pass.

Fixed: the fixture keys its rows 1 and 2, the story comment names the fixture, and the descriptor
notice states that the Open record must exist in the fixture.
